$comment: Modules D and E, the T2 question set (SCRUM-97): eating pattern, dietary approach, exclusions, alcohol, caffeine, training frequency, session length. Asked after week one, on the T2 re-entry surface (SCRUM-98). Every item names its downstream use; nothing the wearable can answer is asked (steps come from the device). Structured answers only. THE OPTION WORDING IS A DEVELOPER DRAFT from the ticket's field list, not from the advisory pack, and needs the content owner's review (plan v2 §9.14) before launch. Items are unscored: none feeds a trait axis.

items.question: How do your meals usually fall on an ordinary day?
options: Three meals at fairly regular times
Two meals, one of them the main one
One main meal and small bits around it
It varies a lot from day to day
items.use: Meal-timing anchor for the scheduler; regularity of the main meal is the lever T5 points at.

items.question: When do you usually first eat something?
items.use: SAFETY SIGNAL, not personalisation: joined with the hypo-risk flag from Module B (SCRUM-96) to say when a late first meal matters. The join is not built until Module B exists.

items.question: Which is closest to how you eat?
items.use: Filters the meal library so nothing suggested is something the subject does not eat.

items.question: Anything you don't eat, or can't?
items.use: Exclusions for the meal library. Dairy is also a controlled food tag the engine can block; wiring exclusions into the food chain is a rulebook change and is not done here.

items.question: How much alcohol in a typical week?
items.use: Context for the recovery layer; never a verdict. Bands rather than units so the answer is honest.

items.question: How much caffeine on a typical day?
items.use: Rule 1.2's no-caffeine-after-midday constraint lands differently for a five-a-day subject; used for how the constraint is worded, never whether it applies.

items.question: How often do you train in a typical week?
How long is a typical session?
items.use: Load progression baseline; sizes the substitute sessions the engine offers.
